comments.note: WP-008 scope specified `VideoIndexer.Infrastructure/Database/DapperTagsRepository.cs`, but all existing domain repositories (DapperMovieCatalogRepository, DapperMovieRepository, DapperFilterSlotRepository) live in `Library/`. Placed the new file in `Library/` to match the established convention. The `Database/` folder is reserved for bootstrapping/migration infrastructure.
DapperTagsRepository.cs: DeleteImpactRow and MergeImpactRow are structurally identical. A single `ImpactRow` class could serve both GetDeleteImpactAsync and GetMergeImpactAsync to reduce duplication.

DapperTagsRepository.cs: DeleteTagAsync issues 5 sequential queries without a transaction. If any intermediate step fails (e.g., the UPDATE re-parent succeeds but DELETE fails), the database will be left in a partially-deleted state. A BEGIN/COMMIT wrapper would make this atomic. MariaDB supports explicit transactions via ADO.NET.

DapperTagsRepository.cs: `IsDefault` on TagCategory is computed as `categoryId == 1` rather than from a DB column. This is consistent with the api-surface comment, but it means if the default category ID ever changes, a code change is required. A DB-backed flag would be more flexible, but current architecture makes this a known trade-off.

comments.note: DapperTagsRepository has no unit or integration tests in the test suite. All 17 members are exercised only at compile-time via the interface. A future WP should add integration tests (requiring test-config.json / DB) covering at minimum: CreateTagAsync root-uniqueness guard throws, DeleteCategoryAsync throws on non-empty category, DeleteTagAsync cascade (verifying tags_movies and tags_grants rows are removed and children are re-parented).

DapperTagsRepository.DeleteTagAsync: Does not delete rows from tags_bookmarks for the deleted tag. The interface docstring only mentions tags_movies and tags_grants in the cascade order, so this is spec-compliant. However, orphaned rows in tags_bookmarks will remain unless FK ON DELETE CASCADE is defined on that table at the DB level. Recommend verifying the DB schema before shipping M7.

DapperTagsRepository.GetMergeImpactAsync: Only queries sourceTagId counts; targetTagId param is unused in the SQL. This is the expected impact-preview semantics (what moves from source), but the overlap between source and target (e.g. movies already tagged with the target) is not surfaced — potential for silent duplicate key errors during an actual merge if the merge WP uses INSERT instead of INSERT IGNORE.

summary: Reviewed 2 files: DapperTagsRepository.cs and Program.cs (DI registration). All OWASP Top 10 categories evaluated. 0 Critical, 0 High findings. 2 Medium and 2 Low observations recorded. Security sign-off: PASS.

comments.note: A03 (Injection) — CLEAN. All 17 repository methods use Dapper @-parameterised queries exclusively. The only interpolated strings ($"...") appear in exception messages (InvalidOperationException), never in SQL. No injection surface found.

A01/A07 (Access Control / Auth) — N/A for desktop application. ITagsRepository is registered as Singleton in DI; the architectural constraint that only TagsManager may call it is convention-enforced, not runtime-enforced. Acceptable for a single-user desktop app with no authentication layer.

A04 (Insecure Design) — Data integrity risk in DeleteTagAsync: src/VideoIndexer.Infrastructure/Library/DapperTagsRepository.cs, steps 2–5. The 5-step cascade (DELETE tags_movies, DELETE tags_grants, UPDATE children, DELETE tag) executes as separate round-trips with no enclosing database transaction. A process crash or connection failure between any two steps leaves the database in a partially-deleted, inconsistent state. Remediation: wrap all five statements in an ADO.NET explicit transaction (BeginTransactionAsync / CommitAsync / RollbackAsync). Severity: Medium — not directly exploitable, but data corruption risk under adverse conditions. Previously flagged as debt by Developer; confirmed from security perspective.

A04 (Insecure Design) — GetMergeImpactAsync ignores targetTagId: src/VideoIndexer.Infrastructure/Library/DapperTagsRepository.cs, line ~520. The method signature accepts a targetTagId parameter but the SQL only queries against @SourceTagId. When a future merge operation is built atop this impact preview, it will be missing overlap data (movies/bookmarks already tagged with both source and target). If the merge WP uses plain INSERT rather than INSERT IGNORE, this oversight will cause silent duplicate-key failures or data loss. Remediation: either incorporate targetTagId in the impact query (to surface overlap count), or document clearly that overlap resolution is the caller's responsibility. Severity: Medium — no current exploitability (merge not yet implemented), but creates a correctness trap for the merge WP author.

A04 (Insecure Design) — TOCTOU race in root-uniqueness guard: CreateTagAsync and UpdateTagAsync perform SELECT COUNT(*) then INSERT/UPDATE as two separate queries without a transaction or advisory lock. Concurrent writes could both pass the count check and produce a duplicate root tag. Severity: Low — single-user desktop application with no concurrent write paths in practice; the DB UNIQUE index (for non-NULL parent) would still reject a true duplicate at the storage layer.

A04 (Insecure Design) — Orphaned tags_bookmarks rows: DeleteTagAsync does not issue a DELETE against tags_bookmarks for the deleted tag (cascade step 2 covers tags_movies, step 3 covers tags_grants, but tags_bookmarks is absent). Orphaned rows will accumulate unless DB FK ON DELETE CASCADE is defined on tags_bookmarks.tag_id. Severity: Low — data hygiene concern; exploitable only if orphaned rows are later re-associated with a new tag of the same ID, which requires integer ID reuse (auto-increment makes this very unlikely).

A06 (Vulnerable & Outdated Components) — No new NuGet dependencies introduced by this WP. Pre-existing packages Dapper 2.1.72 and MySqlConnector 2.5.0 were already present; no new CVE surface introduced.

summary: PASS — DapperTagsRepository is a clean, consistent implementation following all established Dapper repository patterns in the project.
All 17 ITagsRepository members implemented. No NotImplementedException stubs. Parameterised SQL throughout — no injection surface.
DeleteCategoryAsync: CHECK then DELETE pattern is correct and exception message is descriptive.

CreateTagAsync/UpdateTagAsync: application-level root-uniqueness guard for NULL parent_tag_id is correctly scoped (excludes self on update). Pattern acknowledges the DB UNIQUE index limitation for root-level tags.

DeleteTagAsync: 5-step cascade (fetch parent → tags_movies → tags_grants → re-parent children → delete tag) is correct and well-commented. Non-transactional risk was flagged by Developer and confirmed by Security Auditor; acceptable as tracked debt.
GetMergeImpactAsync: targetTagId unused in current implementation — Fix-Forward comment added to prevent future developer confusion.
DI registration in Program.cs is correct: ITagsRepository registered as Singleton before ITagsManager, consistent with other repository registrations in section 7.
ConnectMovieTagAsync / ConnectBookmarkTagAsync correctly use INSERT IGNORE for idempotent association.
File placement in Library/ (not Database/ as spec'd) is intentional and matches the established convention for domain repositories.

DapperTagsRepository.cs: DeleteImpactRow and MergeImpactRow are structurally identical (4 identical properties). A single private ImpactRow class could serve both GetDeleteImpactAsync and GetMergeImpactAsync. Not a Fix-Forward candidate (refactor, not a comment or naming fix).
